name: Matter Milestone Updates

parameters.content:
## Matter Milestone Updates

### How it works

1. The workflow listens for changes in matter status via a webhook and normalizes the incoming data.
2. It verifies webhook handshakes and filters for valid matter status change events.
3. The workflow fetches updated matter and firm user details from Clio, checks if the status actually changed, and looks up a corresponding status update message.
4. If a relevant message exists, it builds and checks compliance of a status update email before sending it to clients who have not opted out.
5. Independently, it runs a daily scheduled check to ensure the Clio webhook subscription is active and renews it if necessary.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Clio API credentials and set CLIO_BASE_URL as a workflow variable.
- [ ] Set up the webhook URL in Clio to trigger "When Matter Status Changes" node.
- [ ] Customize the status update messages in the "Look Up Status Update Message" code node if needed.
- [ ] Ensure compliance sub-workflow referenced by "Check Compliance Before Sending" is properly configured.
- [ ] Provide email sending credentials and configure the "Send Status Update Email" node.

### Customization

Customize the plain-English status update messages in the "Look Up Status Update Message" node to reflect firm-preferred language per Clio matter status.

## Webhook trigger and normalization

Receives and normalizes incoming webhook events for matter status changes.

## Webhook verification and validation

Handles webhook verification handshakes and filters for valid matter events.

## Fetch matter and user details

Fetches detailed data for the matter and firm users from Clio for validation and personalization.

## Check status change detection

Determines if the matter's status has actually changed using static workflow data.

## Lookup and message decision

Looks up the firm-approved status update message and decides if one exists for the changed status.

## Build and compliance check email

Builds the plain-English status update email and invokes a sub-workflow to check compliance before sending.

## Send or skip email

Sends the status update email if approved or skips if the client opted out.

## Daily webhook subscription check

Scheduled daily check to list existing Clio webhooks and decide if renewal is needed.

## Webhook renewal or skip

Registers or renews the Clio webhook if needed or skips if still valid.

nodes.name: When Matter Status Updates
nodes.notes:
Receives Clio's matter status-transition webhook (matter_opened / matter_pended / matter_closed — see 'Register Or Renew Clio Webhook' for why these specific events, not the generic 'updated' event).

Confirmed live: Clio's matter status is a built-in field with exactly three values (Open/Pending/Closed), set on the matter's own detail page — NOT a Task's status, and not any custom field. Changing a Task's status (even one that looks like a workflow stage, e.g. 'In Review'/'In Progress') does nothing here; make sure you're testing against the actual Matter's Status control.

Confirmed live: Clio has no Settings UI for webhook management — registering one is an API-only action, requiring its own Webhooks scope (Read + Write) on your Clio OAuth2 app, granted separately from Matters/Tasks/Users (if you add it after the credential was already authorized, reconnect the credential — same lesson as PAC-64's ForbiddenError). Clio webhooks also EXPIRE (31-day maximum) — not a one-time setup.

Rather than hand-crafting that API call yourself, this template ships with a self-maintaining branch further down the canvas ('Check Webhook Subscription Daily' and the nodes after it) that creates and renews the subscription automatically using this same Clio credential — see that branch's sticky note. Copy THIS node's Production URL (visible after you activate this workflow) into the FIRM_MATTER_WEBHOOK_URL n8n Variable once, and that branch takes care of the rest, including the very first registration (just run it manually via 'Execute step').

Confirmed live: a newly created Clio webhook sits in status 'pending' and delivers NOTHING until a one-time verification handshake succeeds. Immediately after creation (or whenever its URL changes), Clio sends a POST here carrying a unique secret in an X-Hook-Secret header, and expects that exact same secret echoed back in an X-Hook-Secret response header with a 200 — 'a webhook will not be enabled until this handshake is successful' (Clio's own docs). That's why responseMode is 'responseNode' rather than n8n's default immediate response: 'Is Verification Handshake' right after this node detects that header and routes to a dedicated response that echoes it back, separately from the normal event-acknowledgment path.

Do not rely on this node's payload for the matter's current data; only the matter id is trusted from it, and everything else is re-fetched live from Clio. Confirmed live delivery shape: { data: { id, status }, meta: { event, webhook_id } } — the matter id is under body.data.id — but the fetch below is still the authoritative source for status, client, and attorney, not this payload.

Generic practice management systems: POST JSON with a 'matter_id' (or 'id') field; this workflow re-fetches the rest from Clio regardless, so a generic caller only needs to identify which matter changed.

nodes.name: Parse Matter Status Webhook
nodes.notes: Extracts only the matter id from whichever webhook shape arrived, OR detects Clio's verification handshake (an X-Hook-Secret header) and short-circuits to that instead. Confirmed live real Clio delivery shape: body.data.id (matter id), body.data.status (not trusted — re-fetched fresh next), body.meta.event (e.g. 'matter_closed'). is_valid_event is false if no usable matter id was found anywhere in a real event payload — the next node routes that to a labelled Skip rather than continuing with an empty id (the CLAUDE.md guard pattern for external webhooks that fire on more events than the actionable ones).

nodes.name: If Verification Handshake
nodes.notes:
Yes (this call carried Clio's X-Hook-Secret header) → echo it straight back so Clio flips the webhook from 'pending' to active. This is a one-time call per webhook creation (or URL change), not a real matter event — nothing downstream of the main flow runs for it.
No (a normal event delivery, or nothing usable at all) → acknowledge it immediately AND continue into the real matter-event flow in parallel, so Clio's delivery call doesn't wait on the compliance check and email send to finish.

nodes.name: Respond To Handshake Confirmation
nodes.notes: Echoes Clio's own X-Hook-Secret value back in the response header, exactly as Clio's docs require: 'a webhook will not be enabled until this handshake is successful.' Without this, the webhook silently stays in status 'pending' forever and never delivers a single real event — confirmed live the hard way. This fires once per webhook creation (or whenever its URL changes, e.g. after the daily renewal branch creates a fresh one) — not on every matter update.

nodes.name: Respond To Event Acknowledgement
nodes.notes: Sends Clio's real event delivery an immediate 200 so it doesn't time out waiting for the compliance check and email send to finish — the actual processing (matter lookup, dedupe, message lookup, send) continues in parallel via 'If Valid Matter Event' and keeps running after this response is sent.

nodes.name: If Valid Matter Event
nodes.notes:
Yes (a usable matter id was found) → look up the matter's current state.
No (unrecognized payload shape, or no matter id anywhere in it) → route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip Invalid Or Unrelated Event
nodes.notes: This webhook call didn't carry a usable matter id — nothing to look up or notify about. No email sent.

nodes.name: Fetch Matter Details From API
nodes.notes:
Fetches this one matter's authoritative current state directly by id — the webhook payload is never trusted for the actual data, only for which matter to look up. Treating the webhook as a pointer rather than a data source sidesteps uncertainty about exactly what fields Clio includes in the event payload.

Confirmed live: single-resource GET on /matters/{id}.json returns 'status' as a field, wrapped in a 'data' object — same convention as the list endpoints used elsewhere in this catalog.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63/64/65 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From API
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory — used by 'Build Status Update Email' to resolve the matter's responsible_attorney id to a real name and email, so the update can be personalized. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association (Clio rejects a nested User's email — confirmed live in PAC-63).

Runs after the matter fetch in this single linear chain — there's no fan-out from the trigger here, so there's no risk of the disconnected-side-fetch execution problem PAC-63/64 hit; this node is simply the next real step.

Same Clio OAuth2 credential as the matter fetch above — no separate setup.

nodes.name: Check If Matter Status Changed
nodes.notes: Static data is local to this n8n instance's execution store — it won't sync across multiple workers if the instance ever moves to queue mode. Fine for the single-instance deployment this template targets; flag it if the firm later scales to a multi-worker n8n setup.

nodes.name: If Status Actually Changed
nodes.notes:
Yes (status genuinely differs from what this workflow last saw for this matter) → look up whether there's a client message for it.
No (first time seeing this matter, or a redelivered/duplicate event for a status already recorded) → route to Skip.

nodes.name: Skip Unchanged Or First Seen Status
nodes.notes: Either this is a redelivered or duplicate event for a status this workflow already recorded, or this is the first event this workflow has ever seen for this matter. No email sent either way.

nodes.name: Fetch Status Update Message
nodes.notes: The one node every firm must customize before going live — the STATUS_MESSAGES map is the entire content surface of this template. Clio's matter status is exactly Open/Pending/Closed (confirmed live) — no other values are possible unless your firm's Clio instance has a custom setup you've separately verified.

nodes.name: If Status Has Update Message
nodes.notes:
Yes (this status has a firm-approved message configured) → build and send the update.
No (an internal-only or unconfigured status) → route to Skip. No email sent.

nodes.name: Skip No Client Message For Status
nodes.notes: This status genuinely changed, but the firm hasn't configured a client-facing message for it — treated as internal-only. No email sent.

nodes.name: Build Status Update Email
nodes.notes: Do not add an opt-out footer to 'message' (the plain-text body) — the compliance guardrail (next node) appends it automatically to that version and logs the send attempt. 'email_html' carries its own independently-built matching footer, since the guardrail never sees or touches the HTML version.

nodes.name: Execute Compliance Check Workflow
nodes.notes:
Checks whether this client has opted out of firm emails. If not, appends the required unsubscribe footer and logs the send attempt to the audit sheet — same client-facing pattern as PAC-18/64/65.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable.

Returns: { approved, message_out, recipient, suppression_reason } plus all upstream fields — note this REPLACES $json, so any field the build step added (like email_html) is not carried forward automatically; downstream nodes that need it must reach back to $('Build Status Update Email').item.json explicitly (confirmed the hard way in PAC-65 — reading $json.email_html here sent a blank email).

nodes.name: If Update Compliance Approved
nodes.notes:
Yes (client hasn't opted out) → send.
No (client has opted out of firm emails) → route to Skip. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail.

nodes.name: Send Matter Status Email
nodes.notes:
Sends the compliance-approved update to the client — both the plain-text body (message_out from the guardrail, carrying the required unsubscribe footer) and the styled HTML body. HTML and subject both reach back to 'Build Status Update Email' by name rather than reading $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced $json with its own response.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.

nodes.name: Skip Client Opt-Out Status
nodes.notes: This client has opted out of firm emails. The suppression is already logged by the guardrail workflow. No email is sent.

nodes.name: Schedule Daily Webhook Check
nodes.notes:
Runs once a day (3am, n8n server timezone) purely to make sure Clio's webhook subscription is still alive — completely separate from the matter-update branch above. This is what replaces the manual 'POST to Clio's API by hand every few weeks' process: as long as this workflow is Active, the subscription renews itself before it can expire.

You can also trigger this branch manually at any time (click this node, then 'Execute step', then walk each following node the same way) — that's the recommended way to create the webhook for the very first time, since it uses this workflow's own already-authorized Clio credential instead of a hand-crafted API call.

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Clio Webhooks
nodes.notes:
Lists every webhook currently registered on this Clio app, so the next step can tell whether the one this workflow depends on already exists and still has enough life left in it. Same Clio OAuth2 credential as the rest of this workflow — this is what makes self-renewal possible without a separate manual API call: n8n already holds a valid, auto-refreshing OAuth token for this credential.

This is also the safe first node to manually 'Execute step' on when setting up the webhook for the very first time.

nodes.name: Check If Webhook Renewal Needed
nodes.notes: needs_renewal is true if no webhook matches this workflow's own URL and all three status-transition events, the one that does is within 5 days of expiring, OR it's stuck in a non-confirmed status like 'pending' regardless of how far off its expiry is — confirmed live that a webhook can sit in 'pending' with a perfectly healthy-looking expires_at forever if its verification handshake never succeeded. stuck_pending_webhook_id surfaces the old broken subscription's id for visibility (it isn't deleted automatically — Clio will let it expire on its own).

nodes.name: If Webhook Needs Renewal
nodes.notes:
Yes (missing, or expiring within 5 days) → (re)register it with Clio.
No (already valid with plenty of life left) → route to Skip. Nothing to do today.

nodes.name: Skip Valid Webhook Status
nodes.notes: The webhook this workflow depends on already exists and isn't close to expiring. Nothing to do today.

nodes.name: Register Or Renew Clio Webhook
nodes.notes:
Creates a fresh Clio webhook subscription for this workflow's own URL, valid for another 31 days (Clio's maximum). This is the same API call that used to require a hand-crafted curl/Postman request outside n8n — now it just runs automatically before the old one can expire, using the credential already wired up for every other Clio call in this workflow.

Subscribes to matter_opened, matter_pended, and matter_closed specifically — Clio's own dedicated events for matter status transitions — rather than the generic 'updated' event. Confirmed live that Clio's actual matter status field only has three values (Open/Pending/Closed, set on the matter's own detail page, not a Task's status or any custom field), and Clio's docs describe these three event names as firing 'whenever a matter's status changes to' each value. This is more precise than watching 'updated' with a fields filter and avoids firing on unrelated edits at all.

The target URL comes from the FIRM_MATTER_WEBHOOK_URL n8n Variable, set once during deployment (copy it from the 'When Matter Status Changes' node's Production URL tab) — n8n can't read a webhook node's own public URL back out via an expression, so this one manual copy-paste is unavoidable, but it only has to happen once, not every 31 days.

Check this node's output after it runs (or the Executions tab) to confirm Clio returned a new webhook id and expires_at rather than an error — if your Clio OAuth2 app doesn't have the Webhooks (Read + Write) scope granted and the credential reconnected afterward, this call fails with the same ForbiddenError pattern confirmed in PAC-64.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { url: $vars.FIRM_MATTER_WEBHOOK_URL, model: 'matter', events: ['matter_opened', 'matter_pended', 'matter_closed'], fields: 'id,status', expires_at: $now.plus({ days: 31 }).toISO() } }) }}

main.node: Skip Unchanged Or First Seen Status
Skip No Client Message For Status

description: Fires on Clio's matter status-transition webhooks (matter_opened / matter_pended / matter_closed — Clio's built-in matter status is exactly Open/Pending/Closed), trusting only the matter id from the payload — everything else is re-fetched live from Clio (current status, client, responsible attorney). Compares the fetched status against the last one this workflow saw for the matter, using n8n's own workflow static data (no external database), so a client update only sends on a genuine status change, never a duplicate. Looks the new status up in a firm-edited, plain-English message map — an unconfigured status is treated as internal-only and skipped. Sends the matching update, personalized with the assigned attorney's name where resolvable, through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail. Replaces a paid Case Status app — poor communication between milestones is a top bar-complaint driver of client dissatisfaction.

meta.name: Send client matter status updates from Clio via webhooks and SMTP email
